h1: Retatrutide: the doses used in trials, what the weight-loss numbers actually were, and the trials still running
dek: A triple GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist that no regulator has approved. This page tables every registered trial by its ClinicalTrials.gov number as the published paper states it, gives the dose-response from the phase 2 obesity trial at 24 and 48 weeks as published, and separates the doses that were studied from the ones that circulate.

queries.heading: Retatrutide and tirzepatide, and why the headline percentages do not compare
The escalation schedules the trials used
queries.boundary: Trials escalated from a starting dose over weeks. The starting dose itself changed the side-effect rate, which is why it is reported here rather than only the target dose.

queries.heading: Reconstitution arithmetic, and what the trials say about it
Is retatrutide approved?
queries.answer: No regulator has approved retatrutide for any use. It is an investigational molecule in phase 3 trials. Anything sold as retatrutide today is sold outside an approved supply chain.

information_gain: The only page that tables every registered retatrutide trial by the ClinicalTrials.gov number the published paper itself declares, alongside phase, enrolment and what the trial reported, so a reader can tell a completed phase 3 from a design paper for trials that have not read out. None of the three scored competitors cites a single registration. It is also the only page giving the phase 2 obesity dose-response as published at both 24 and 48 weeks for all four dose groups against placebo, rather than quoting the single best number; the only one reporting that the starting dose, not the target dose, is what changed the side-effect rate; and the only one carrying the dose-dependent heart-rate increase that peaked at 24 weeks and then declined, which every competitor omits.
serp_format_rewarded: Dosage queries return an AI overview plus listicle-style guides with H3-heavy structure and no tables. A table that names the trial behind each dose is both the format the query wants and the thing no incumbent has. The side-effects query returns four results, none from a health publisher, so a cited adverse-events section can take it outright.
open_actions: Trial registry pages on clinicaltrials.gov and the DailyMed label at rank 5 could not be retrieved: the sandbox that built this page reaches Europe PMC but not clinicaltrials.gov, dailymed.nlm.nih.gov or api.fda.gov. Every NCT number here is quoted from the published paper that declares it. Re-verify against the registry from an environment with access before treating the registry as a source in its own right.

DailyMed carries a retatrutide entry at rank 5 for 'retatrutide dosage'. Retatrutide has no FDA approval, so that listing needs checking: it is most likely an unapproved compounded preparation, which would itself be worth a cited paragraph.
